QEVA CORE 0.2
=============

PURPOSE
This file is a compact, human-readable description of the QEVA record model.
It is normative where it is stricter than explanatory web pages. The JSON
Schema is an interoperability aid; QEVA does not require future readers to
possess a JSON-Schema implementation.

IDENTITY
A logical object has a stable id such as:
  qeva:1:sequence
A released revision is addressed exactly as:
  qeva:1:sequence@1
Dependencies, assumptions that use a QEVA record, relations, framework_ref,
and supersedes MUST use exact revision references. An old record must never
silently acquire the meaning of a newer dependency revision.

RECORD
Every record contains:
  qeva_version   protocol version
  id             stable logical object id
  revision       positive integer revision
  kind           record class; type is not part of identity
  title          human label
  summary        short orientation text
  domains        non-normative discovery tags
  context        mathematical framework and optional exact framework_ref
  assumptions    explicit assumptions; each may have an exact QEVA ref
  content        plain explanation, exact formulation, example, caveat
  dependencies   exact QEVA revision refs needed to interpret the record
  relations      typed exact links to other QEVA revisions
  verification   what checking has actually occurred
  provenance     origin, date, license, source note
  supersedes     exact prior revision, or null
  legacy_ids     historical identifiers retained for migration

PROOF AND TRUTH
Gamma |-_{S} P is syntactic derivability: P has a permitted finite proof in
formal system S from premises Gamma.
M |= P is semantic satisfaction: P holds in model M under declared semantics.
QEVA MUST NOT collapse these into one unlabeled Boolean field called true.

IMMUTABILITY
Once released, the bytes and meaning of an object revision are historical.
Corrections create a new revision. The new revision points to the exact old
revision through supersedes.

ENCODING
Archive JSON is JSON as standardized by RFC 8259 and encoded as UTF-8 as in
RFC 3629, without a byte-order mark. Generated JSONL contains one complete
JSON object per LF-terminated line. Canonical JSON used for per-record digests
sorts object keys lexicographically, emits no insignificant whitespace, emits
Unicode characters directly as UTF-8, and appends one LF byte.

HASHES
Digests provide fixity, not timeless semantic identity and not authorship.
Release 0.2 emits SHA-256 and SHA-512 manifests. Later releases may add other
algorithms. Old manifests remain historical artifacts.

END QEVA CORE 0.2
